For executives

The answer is in the report. It is buried under controls, slow loads and missing dollars.

A CEO’s first 30 seconds in a report, today

Org Health report, opened from Home. This is when an executive either engages or asks for a walkthrough.

SecondWhat they seeWhat they need
0–6

“Loading report N%” counter, tabs disabled

The brief, rendered first

6–10

Page title, marketing subtitle, filters, 6 AI chips, 6 tabs

Company · read · date · n, in one line

10–15

Yellow “Executive summary may be outdated… Regenerate”

Nothing, or “Generated 12 Oct”

15–30

The start of a 110-word headline at ~190 characters per line. Findings and actions below the fold, in two columns

One-sentence headline with value at stake; three rows of finding → action → owner → due

By second 30 the reader has half a paragraph and no action. That’s why reports need a person to walk executives through them.

Part 2 of 3

For HR

The AI pieces of setup exist. They don’t carry through to launch.

Today the AI is six features, and all of them wait to be asked

The “third partner” exists as features, not behaviour. There is no single place where the AI proposes and the user approves.

Six separate entry points
Report AI chips

“Draft board memo”, “Brief CHRO”… six chips above the headline

Entrolina chat

Strong on results; wrong UI labels on how-to questions

Template “describe needs”

Its recommendation isn’t carried into the survey

Business Context

Extraction with no visible output

“Enable AI summaries”

A per-tab toggle; Top Comments says AI is disabled

Regenerate

Shown to every reader, in admin language

They behave differently and share no context. The fix is one assistant with three modes: explain, draft, propose.

Where the AI should step in

The AI does the preparation at the right moment. The person decides with one click.

Choosing the read

Results ready

Report walkthrough

Next finding · assign owner

Rule of thumb: AI prepares, the UI confirms. Clicking stays first-class, and anything irreversible is an explicit click.
